Netflix Research

# Recommendations

## Figuring out how to bring unique joy to each member

## About

Welcome to the Netflix information hub for Personalization, Recommendations and Search research. This page showcases our journey in enhancing member experiences through the research and application of state-of-the-art technologies.

Recommendation and Search algorithms are at the heart of Netflix's services. They are pivotal in providing our members around the world with personalized entertainment suggestions that align with their preferences at any given moment. Recognizing the critical role these recommendations play, we are committed to continuous improvement and advancement in this field.

Personalization starts on the homepage and extends beyond our product. This includes personalized messaging and app notifications to keep members informed and engaged. Recognizing the variety of our customer’s needs, our advanced search features are designed to empower members to efficiently navigate our catalog, allowing them to find the right videos and games. This includes addressing the challenges associated with accommodating numerous languages and handling diverse input mechanisms from various devices, such as TV remotes and voice controls. We also extend our work beyond the title selection layer by looking for new ways we can present recommendations, explain them, and have members interact with our systems. Our goal is to minimize the time browsing and searching while maximizing enjoyment.

While our research has made many significant improvements to recommendation systems over the years, there is still a long way to go until every member is given the perfect recommendation at the top of their page while understanding why it will be great for them. Thus, we continue to improve our algorithms while looking for new areas we can personalize. We conduct research in areas of machine learning with the goal to make member experience better. Our work on recommender systems, contextual bandits, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, foundational models, and causal inference is published at leading conferences. 

We invite you to explore our collection of research, including papers, blog posts, and case studies. Each piece offers insights into the practical applications and future potential of our work in personalization, recommendations and search.
